__default__.symptoms: Visible leaf damage detected. Consult a local agronomist for confirmation.
chemical: Consult local agricultural extension office for recommended fungicides

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety lesions on leaves; corky scab lesions on fruit; severe defoliation
organic: Collect and destroy fallen leaves in autumn
Apply lime sulfur spray at silver-tip stage
Urea foliar spray on fallen leaves reduces overwintering spores
prevention: Complete spray programme from green tip to petal fall

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Circular purple-bordered lesions on leaves ('frog-eye leaf spot'); mummified fruit with black rot; cankers on branches
organic: Prune and destroy infected branches and mummified fruit
Remove dead wood that harbors the fungus
prevention: Remove mummified fruit and cankers before dormancy
Maintain tree vigor with balanced nutrition

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surface; tube-like aecia on leaf underside; distorted fruit
organic: Remove nearby eastern red cedar (Juniperus virginiana) hosts if feasible
Apply sulfur-based spray from pink stage through petal fall
chemical: Myclobutanil 20WP — 0.5 g/L at pink through petal fall
prevention: Avoid planting apple trees near cedars/junipers
Begin spray programme at tight-cluster stage

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Water at soil level — avoid wetting foliage
prevention: Rotate spray materials to prevent resistance

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Monitor for mummy berry and mildew
Maintain soil pH 4.5–5.5 for optimal health
Mulch with pine bark to retain moisture

Cherry___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal growth on young leaves and shoots; distorted curled leaves; reduced fruit set
organic: Apply potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) as foliar spray
Spray dilute milk solution (1:9 ratio) weekly
chemical: Sulfur 80WG — 3 g/L (do not apply in heat >30°C)
prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen — promotes susceptible growth

Cherry___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
prevention: Scout for brown rot and leaf spot

Corn___Cercospora_leaf_spot.symptoms: Rectangular grey-tan lesions with distinct parallel margins along leaf veins; lesions may merge causing blighting
organic: Avoid stress (water, nutrients) that increases susceptibility
prevention: Reduce surface residue in conservation-till systems

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Cinnamon-brown pustules (uredinia) scattered on both leaf surfaces; later turn black (telia)
prevention: Avoid late planting into high-risk periods

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long (5–15 cm) elliptical grey-green to tan cigar-shaped lesions on leaves; severe in cool-wet conditions

Corn___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Monitor for early rust or blight pustules
prevention: Rotate with soybean or other broadleaves
Scout at V6 and tasselling stages

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular spots on leaves; shriveled mummified black berries
organic: Remove mummified berries and infected canes
Apply copper hydroxide (2 g/L) — key timing at bud break
Ensure good canopy airflow by pruning
prevention: Remove all mummified fruit before dormancy
Spray programme from bud break to berry set

Grape___Esca_Black_Measles.symptoms: Tiger-stripe leaf discolouration (yellow/red margins, green centre); dark berry spots ('measles'); internal wood streaking
organic: Prune infected wood back to clean tissue
Seal pruning wounds immediately with wound sealant
Remove and destroy severely affected vines
chemical: Wound protectants: Trichoderma-based products at pruning
Avoid spreading through contaminated pruning tools — disinfect with 70% ethanol
prevention: Prune in dry weather to reduce infection risk
Avoid large pruning wounds — staggered pruning reduces stress

Grape___Leaf_blight.symptoms: Angular dark brown lesions on upper leaf surface; grey powdery growth on underside; premature defoliation
organic: Improve canopy ventilation through leaf removal
prevention: Maintain open canopy with shoot positioning

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Balanced potassium fertilisation for berry quality
prevention: Maintain spray calendar for powdery and downy mildew

Orange___Haunglongbing.cause: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (bacterium) — spread by Asian citrus psyllid
Orange___Haunglongbing.symptoms: Asymmetric yellow mottling ('blotchy mottle'); small lopsided fruit; bitter hollow fruit with aborted seeds; die-back
organic: Remove and destroy infected trees to prevent spread
Control Asian citrus psyllid with reflective mulch
Introduce psyllid parasitoids (Tamarixia radiata) where available
chemical: No curative treatment — infected trees must be removed
Psyllid control: Imidacloprid 70WG soil drench — 1 g/L

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular water-soaked leaf spots with yellow halo; shot-hole appearance as lesions fall out; sunken fruit lesions
organic: Apply copper hydroxide (2 g/L) from petal fall to hull split — preventive
chemical: Copper oxychloride 50WP — 2 g/L (6–8 sprays from shuck split)
prevention: Avoid sites with high rainfall during pit hardening

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Continue monitoring for bacterial spot and brown rot
prevention: Dormant copper spray before bud swell

Pepper___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked lesions with yellow halo on leaves; raised scab-like spots on fruit
organic: Remove and destroy infected plant material
Apply copper hydroxide (2 g/L) — preventive only
chemical: Streptomycin sulfate 17WP — 0.6 g/L (regulated — check local rules)

Pepper___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Monitor for aphids and mites — vectors for viruses

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings (target-board appearance) on older leaves
organic: Apply compost tea as foliar spray
Ensure balanced nutrition — potassium deficiency worsens severity

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems; white sporulation on underside; tuber rot in severe cases
organic: Apply Bordeaux mixture (1%) at first sign

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Continue monitoring for late blight during cool-wet weather

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Monitor for cane blight and spur blight
Prune out old floricanes after harvest
prevention: Remove wild raspberries nearby — virus reservoir
Good drainage to prevent Phytophthora root rot

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Monitor for soybean rust and sudden death syndrome
Inoculate with Bradyrhizobium for nitrogen fixation
prevention: Use certified seed with seed treatment

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery fungal colonies on upper leaf surface; yellowing and premature senescence; reduced fruit size
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen — promotes lush susceptible growth

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small irregular purplish spots coalescing into large scorched areas; severe defoliation in humid conditions
organic: Remove and destroy infected leaves after harvest
Improve air circulation — avoid dense planting
prevention: Renovate beds after harvest — remove old foliage

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
organic: Monitor for grey mould (Botrytis) during fruiting
Remove runners to maintain plant vigour
Mulch to prevent soil splash onto fruit

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked leaf spots with yellow halo; raised corky spots on green fruit; severe leaf drop
prevention: Sanitise tools and trays between plantings

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown target-ring lesions on older/lower leaves; yellow halo around spots; premature defoliation
organic: Apply neem oil spray (5 mL/L) every 10 days
Mulch to prevent spore splash from soil

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Dark brown water-soaked lesions with pale green border; white mould on leaf undersides in humid conditions
organic: Remove and destroy infected plant parts immediately
Avoid overhead watering — water at soil level
Improve plant spacing for air circulation
prevention: Use certified blight-resistant varieties (e.g. Mountain Merit)

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surface; olive-green to brown velvety mold on underside; defoliation in severe cases
organic: Improve greenhouse ventilation to reduce humidity below 85%
prevention: Use resistant varieties (e.g. Cf-2, Cf-4 genes)
Ensure 1.2 m between rows in greenhouse
Keep humidity below 85% — use ventilation and heating

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark border and grey centre on lower leaves; tiny black pycnidia visible in lesion centre; severe defoliation from bottom up
organic: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves
Apply copper hydroxide (2 g/L) at first sign
prevention: Stake plants to keep foliage off ground

Tomato___Spider_mites.symptoms: Fine stippling (bronze/silvery) on upper leaf surface; webbing on underside; mites visible under 10× lens; severe: leaf drop
organic: Spray with insecticidal soap (5 mL/L) every 5 days
High-pressure water spray to dislodge mites
Neem oil (5 mL/L) as contact miticide
prevention: Monitor regularly, especially in hot dry conditions
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies
Adequate irrigation to reduce plant stress

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings and yellow halo; lesions on leaves, stems and fruit; defoliation from bottom up
organic: Improve airflow — stake plants and prune suckers

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Begomovirus — transmitted by silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe stunting; upward leaf curling with yellow margins; flower drop; near-total yield loss if infected young
organic: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Control whitefly with yellow sticky traps (40/ha)
chemical: No curative treatment — remove infected plants
Imidacloprid 70WG — 0.5 g/L soil drench for whitefly
prevention: Use TYLCV-resistant varieties (e.g. TY-1, Ty-3 genes)
Plant barrier crops (maize) to reduce viruliferous whitefly pressure

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mosaic pattern (light/dark green patches) on leaves; leaf distortion; stunted growth; reduced yield
organic: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost)
Control aphid populations with insecticidal soap
chemical: No curative chemical treatment — prevention only
Imidacloprid 70WG for aphid vector control — 0.5 g/L

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with no visible signs of infection
